If you've been missing the ability to double-click the Digital Crown on your Apple Watch to bring up the app switcher since watchOS 27, it looks like that feature is making a return starting with watchOS 27.2 beta 2. Here's what you need to know.

Apple works to bring back the watchOS app switcher

Apple today released watchOS 27.2 beta 2 to developers, less than a week after the previous beta 1 was released.

Today's beta includes one detail that is likely to be welcomed by a group of long-time Apple Watch users, including my colleague Zac Hall. He wrote an article earlier this month about how watchOS 27 removed the ability to quickly switch between recently used apps by double-clicking the Digital Crown.

His article noted that, at the time, there was no longer any way to quickly jump back to a recent app, and he hoped Apple would bring the gesture back before watchOS 27 was officially released or in a future update.

While Apple did not restore the Digital Crown app switcher shortcut in this watchOS 27.2 beta 2 build, it has reintroduced the app switcher through a new gesture.

As discovered on the Apple Den Discord server and shared by user Bones on X, watchOS 27.2 beta 2 allows users to long-press the bottom of the screen while using an app to bring up the app switcher.

As Bones noted in the post, the rest of the app switcher experience works largely as it did before: after launching the app switcher with a long-press on the bottom of the screen, users can rotate the Digital Crown to scroll through recently used apps, or swipe left on an app and tap the "X" button to remove it from the switcher.

As with any beta, this particular method may not carry over to the final release (which is expected next month), but its inclusion in watchOS 27.2 beta 2 shows Apple is listening to user feedback and working to bring back the app switcher.

Have you missed the app switcher on watchOS 27? Feel free to share with us in the comments.
